e2e4 c7c6.white: Build a pawn center with d4. You can advance, exchange, or keep the tension when Black plays ...d5.
e2e4 c7c6.black: Prepare ...d5 with the c-pawn. Keep the c8 bishop free to develop before ...e6.

ideas.d2d4: Builds a two-pawn center before Black challenges e4.

e2e4 c7c6 d2d4 d7d5.white: Choose the pawn structure. e5 gains space, exd5 opens lines, and Nc3 develops while keeping the tension.
e2e4 c7c6 d2d4 d7d5.black: White’s decision on e4 tells you where to put the c8 bishop and how to challenge the center.

ideas.e4e5: Gains kingside space and drives the game toward a closed center.
ideas.b1c3: Develops the knight and gives e4 more support.

e2e4 c7c6 d2d4 d7d5 e4e5.white: The e5 pawn gives you space. Develop behind the pawn chain and keep an eye on its base at d4.
e2e4 c7c6 d2d4 d7d5 e4e5.black: Develop the c8 bishop with ...Bf5 before ...e6. A later ...c5 challenges d4.

ideas.c8f5: Gets the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain before ...e6.
ideas.c6c5: Challenges d4 immediately with the c-pawn.

e2e4 c7c6 d2d4 d7d5 e4e5 c8f5.white: Develop with Nf3 to support d4, or use another setup that keeps the center intact.
e2e4 c7c6 d2d4 d7d5 e4e5 c8f5.black: Your light-squared bishop is out. Support d5 with ...e6 and look for a chance to play ...c5.

ideas.g1f3: Develops the knight and adds a defender to d4.
ideas.h2h4: Gains space on the kingside and threatens to chase the f5 bishop with g4.

e2e4 c7c6 d2d4 d7d5 e4d5 c6d5.white: Bd3 aims at h7. Develop the knight and castle before looking for a kingside attack.
e2e4 c7c6 d2d4 d7d5 e4d5 c6d5.black: Develop around the half-open c-file. Consider bringing out the c8 bishop before ...e6.

ideas.f1d3: Develops with the bishop already looking toward h7.

e2e4 e7e5 g1f3 b8c6 f1c4.white: Your bishop points at f7. Castle and prepare a central break with c3 and d4 if Black gives you time.
e2e4 e7e5 g1f3 b8c6 f1c4.black: Match White’s development. ...Bc5 eyes f2, while ...Nf6 attacks e4 and invites sharper play.

ideas.f8c5: Develops the bishop with pressure on f2.
ideas.g8f6: Attacks e4 and starts the Two Knights Defense.

e2e4 e7e5 g1f3 b8c6 f1c4 f8c5.white: Prepare d4 with c3, or choose a slower setup with d3 and castling.
e2e4 e7e5 g1f3 b8c6 f1c4 f8c5.black: Develop ...Nf6 and castle. If White prepares d4, pay attention to the tension around e5.

ideas.c2c3: Supports a later d4 break and clears c2 for the bishop to retreat through b3.
ideas.d2d3: Protects e4 and frees the c1 bishop while keeping the center flexible.
ideas.b2b4: Offers a pawn to gain time for c3 and d4 in the Evans Gambit.

e2e4 e7e5 g1f3 b8c6 f1c4 g8f6.white: d3 protects e4 and keeps the game quiet. Ng5 doubles the attack on f7 and invites a sharp central reply.
e2e4 e7e5 g1f3 b8c6 f1c4 g8f6.black: The knight attacks e4. Against Ng5, challenge the center with ...d5.

ideas.d2d3: Supports e4 and opens a diagonal for the c1 bishop.
ideas.f3g5: Adds the knight to the bishop’s attack on f7.

d2d4 d7d5 c2c4 e7e6.white: Put pressure on d5 with Nc3. Exchanging on d5 is another way to define the pawn structure.
d2d4 d7d5 c2c4 e7e6.black: Keep the d5 pawn supported, develop ...Nf6 and ...Be7, then look for a way to free the c8 bishop.

ideas.b1c3: Develops the knight and increases pressure on d5.
ideas.c4d5: Forces Black to decide how to restore the d5 pawn.

d2d4 d7d5 c2c4 e7e6 c4d5 e6d5.name: Queen’s Gambit Declined: Exchange Variation
d2d4 d7d5 c2c4 e7e6 c4d5 e6d5.white: Develop first. A later b4–b5 can create a target in Black’s queenside pawns.
d2d4 d7d5 c2c4 e7e6 c4d5 e6d5.black: Develop toward e4 and consider a central break or active piece play before White advances on the queenside.

ideas.b1c3: Develops the knight toward the central d5 and e4 squares.

d2d4 d7d5 c2c4 e7e6 b1c3 g8f6.white: Bg5 pins the knight to the queen. Develop the kingside and castle before opening the center.
d2d4 d7d5 c2c4 e7e6 b1c3 g8f6.black: Prepare to castle with ...Be7. Leave the d5 tension in place until a trade or a break helps development.

ideas.c1g5: Pins the f6 knight to Black’s queen.
ideas.c4d5: Changes the central pawn structure before developing the bishop.

d2d4 g8f6 c2c4 e7e6 b1c3 f8b4.white: The c3 knight is pinned to your king. e3 develops toward castling, while Qc2 prepares to recapture on c3 with the queen.
d2d4 g8f6 c2c4 e7e6 b1c3 f8b4.black: Use the pin to control e4. Decide whether to keep the bishop or trade it for structural changes on the c-file.

ideas.e2e3: Supports d4 and opens the f1 bishop’s diagonal.
ideas.d1c2: Supports c3 so the queen can recapture if Black trades there.
